description: Choose the profiler for the evidence you need. Discovery inventories metadata; languages retains Linguist-compatible output; all combines languages and ecosystem hints with explicitly selected optional modules. Git repository roots use committed HEAD unless --source directory is selected. No heavier profiler is enabled by choosing this group.
name: analyze

runtime.help_excerpt:
Choose the profiler for the evidence you need. Discovery inventories metadata; languages retains Linguist-compatible output; all combines languages and ecosystem hints with explicitly selected optional modules. Git repository roots use committed HEAD unless --source directory is selected. No heavier profiler is enabled by choosing this group.

Usage:
  dircue analyze [flags]
  dircue analyze [command]

Examples:
  dircue analyze discovery --json /checkout
  dircue analyze languages --source directory --json /content
  dircue analyze all --declarations --metrics --json /checkout

Available Commands:
  all          Combine language statistics, ecosystem hints, and selected profilers
  availability Inspect source-acquisition boundaries without fetching content
  declarations Read static project declarations and named interfaces
  discovery    Inventory file metadata and candidate manifests or artifacts
  ecosystems   Report ecosystems inferred from supported filename and manifest hints
  environments Map declared project environments without running builds
  explain      Explain one file decision or retained project relationship
  focus        Profile a declared project with its original-root context
  formats      Inspect bounded content for format evidence
  frameworks   Report frameworks inferred from supported filename and manifest hints
  graph        Describe static .NET project-reference graphs
  languages    Classify source languages with Linguist-compatible statistics
  metrics      Count lines, comments, code, and lexical complexity with scc
  packages     Import an existing Syft JSON report with project context
  projects     Discover supported project manifests and shared build inputs
  registries   Observe selected NuGet and npm package-source declarations
  rules        Apply explicit rules to selected file metadata and bounded content
  structure    Measure supported syntax through an explicitly supplied native worker

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for analyze

Global Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")
  -r, --rev string           Git revision to analyze (default "HEAD")
      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)

Use "dircue analyze [command] --help" for more information about a command.

side_effects: Only structure, or all --structure, executes an explicitly supplied worker; other commands read only. No inspected code is executed.

Simply type dircue help [path to command] for full details.
name: help

runtime.help_excerpt:
Help provides help for any command in the application.
Simply type dircue help [path to command] for full details.

Usage:
  dircue help [command] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for help

Global Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")
  -r, --rev string           Git revision to analyze (default "HEAD")
      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)

side_effects: Only structure, or all --structure, executes an explicitly supplied worker; other commands read only. No inspected code is executed.

description: Read a saved aggregate profile and plan only the requested follow-ups. Never scans its declared root, probes tools, or executes planned commands. Revalidate source identity, boundary, and freshness before replacing any argv placeholder.
name: plan

runtime.help_excerpt:
Read a saved aggregate profile and plan only the requested follow-ups. Never scans its declared root, probes tools, or executes planned commands. Revalidate source identity, boundary, and freshness before replacing any argv placeholder.

Modules: availability, declarations, discovery, environments, focus, formats, metrics, structure.
Questions: source-availability, project-declarations, content-inventory, environments, project-scope, content-formats, code-metrics, source-structure.

Usage:
  dircue plan <report.json> [flags]

Examples:
  dircue analyze discovery --json /checkout > first-pass.json
  dircue plan first-pass.json --module declarations --json
  dircue plan first-pass.json --question content-formats --json
  dircue plan first-pass.json --module structure --input structural-worker --json

Flags:
  -h, --help                  help for plan
      --input strings         Caller-supplied prerequisite name, such as structural-worker (repeatable)
      --module strings        Planner-supported module to consider (repeatable)
      --project stringArray   Root-relative project selector for focus planning
      --question strings      Follow-up question to consider (repeatable)

Global Flags:
  -j, --json   Emit JSON

side_effects: Only structure, or all --structure, executes an explicitly supplied worker; other commands read only. No inspected code is executed.
